title: The Roof, the Teeth, and the Grid Closed
label: ch:bn-roof-teeth-grid
canDo: I can write the five consonants that finish Bengali's stop grid, hear the breath that separates চ from ছ, read আছি off the page, and say every consonant I own by where in the mouth it is made rather than by what it looks like.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes by reciting ten consonants back from their places of articulation rather than from their shapes, which is the difference between holding a grid and holding a list.
